project: BuildDesk AI Security Defenses & Internal Penetration Testing
description: Comprehensive security hardening initiative driven by analysis of autonomous AI penetration testing tools like Shannon (github.com/KeygraphHQ/shannon). Shannon is an AI-powered pentest framework that autonomously reads source code, identifies vulnerabilities, and executes live exploits against running applications - achieving 96% success rates. It targets XSS, SQL injection, SSRF, broken auth/authz, and command injection using code-aware dynamic testing. This PRD addresses two critical needs: (1) Harden our attack surface against the specific vectors Shannon exploits - removing CSP unsafe directives, adding CSRF/SSRF/rate-limiting protections, and preventing error information leakage, and (2) Build internal security testing capabilities that mirror Shannon's methodology so we can continuously test ourselves. Current gaps: CSP uses unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval, zero CSRF protection, no SSRF prevention in 166+ edge functions, rate limiting is UI-only with no enforcement, and no automated security test suites.

userStories.title: Create SSRF prevention utility with URL allowlisting
userStories.description: As a security engineer, I want a server-side request forgery (SSRF) prevention utility so that our edge functions cannot be tricked into making requests to internal networks or unintended hosts. Shannon specifically targets SSRF vulnerabilities by analyzing code that makes outbound HTTP requests based on user input. Create src/lib/security/ssrfPrevention.ts with: (1) a validateUrl() function that checks URLs against an allowlist of permitted domains and blocks private IP ranges (10.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x, 127.x, 0.0.0.0, ::1, fd00::/8), (2) a sanitizeUrl() function that normalizes URLs to prevent bypass techniques (double encoding, IPv6 embedding, DNS rebinding via octal/hex IP notation, URL parser differentials), (3) a ALLOWED_EXTERNAL_DOMAINS constant with our known integrations (stripe.com, supabase.co, quickbooks.api.intuit.com, googleapis.com, graph.microsoft.com), (4) detection of redirect-based SSRF (flag URLs with redirect parameters). Create comprehensive tests at src/lib/security/__tests__/ssrfPrevention.test.ts.

userStories.title: Harden Content Security Policy by removing unsafe-eval
userStories.description: As a security engineer, I want to remove unsafe-eval from our CSP so that Shannon-style XSS attacks cannot execute arbitrary JavaScript via eval(), Function(), or setTimeout(string). Currently public/_headers has both 'unsafe-inline' and 'unsafe-eval' in the script-src directive, which effectively disables CSP protection against XSS - the #1 attack vector Shannon targets. Remove 'unsafe-eval' from script-src. This may break some third-party libraries that use eval - if so, use 'unsafe-hashes' with specific script hashes instead. Keep 'unsafe-inline' for now (US-003 addresses it). Also add: (1) require-trusted-types-for 'script' directive to prevent DOM XSS, (2) block-all-mixed-content directive, (3) upgrade-insecure-requests if not already present. Test that the build still produces valid HTML.

userStories.title: Add CSRF token protection for state-changing operations
userStories.description: As a security engineer, I want CSRF protection so that attackers cannot forge requests on behalf of authenticated users. Shannon handles complex auth flows and specifically tests for CSRF vulnerabilities. Our current app has ZERO CSRF protection - relying solely on JWT in the Authorization header, which is safe for API calls but NOT for any form submissions or same-origin requests where cookies are sent automatically.
